LESSON: SOIL CONSERVATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: CONSERVATION OF RESOURCES Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes Suggested
Topic 1.1: Soil Conservation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Soil Conservation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we improve the soil using suitable organic wastes?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community
2. construct organic waste pit for soil improvement

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SOIL CONSERVATION
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Soil Conservation helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: SOIL CONSERVATION
Soil Conservation is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community

What this means
In this part you learn to identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil Conservation” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct organic waste pit for soil improvement

What this means
In this part you learn to construct organic waste pit for soil improvement. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct organic waste pit for soil improvement.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Soil Conservation matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct organic waste pit for soil improvement. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Soil Conservation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Soil Conservation” around your school. (skill: identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community)

Example 2: Say why Soil Conservation matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: construct organic waste pit for soil improvement)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Soil Conservation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community.
3. Practise this skill: construct organic waste pit for soil improvement.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Soil Conservation from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Soil Conservation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Soil Conservation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we improve the soil using suitable organic wastes?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Soil Conservation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community.
5. Be able to: construct organic waste pit for soil improvement.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
